svg.title: What this site measures about its own accessibility, and what it does not
svg.desc: On one side, the things computed on every push: contrast for every reviewed colour pair in both themes, resolved from the stylesheet rather than asserted, and structural facts about every built page such as a language, one h1, a main landmark, labelled controls, named buttons, discernible link text, and scoped table headers. On the other side, the things no check here establishes: whether a page reads well to a screen reader, focus order and visibility, captions or transcripts for the archived recordings, reflow at four hundred percent zoom, and whether any status is carried by hue alone. Both are published, because a pass rate without its exclusions is not a usable claim.
svg.text: A pass rate without its exclusions is not a claim anybody can use. Both halves are published.

g.text: Computed on every push
Contrast for every reviewed pair, in both themes,
resolved from the stylesheet, not asserted.
Every built page: a language, one h1, a main
landmark, labelled controls, named buttons,
link text, and scoped table headers.
Below threshold means a red build
The check and this page share one implementation of the
contrast maths, so the published number and the enforced
number cannot disagree.
Not established by any of it
Whether a page actually reads well aloud.
Focus order and focus visibility, page by page.
Captions or transcripts for archived recordings.
Reflow at 400 percent zoom, and text spacing.
Whether a status is carried by hue alone.
Correct structure is necessary, not sufficient
A heading can be present and unhelpful. Alt text can exist
and describe the wrong thing. These need a person, and a
report from one is worth more than any number here.

svg.text: Both columns are generated and published as JSON, including the right-hand one.
